title: On-shell renormalization of sine-Gordon by the quantum inverse scattering method
abstract: In the quantum inverse scattering method, the sine-Gordon model is solved on a lattice, and its continuum and infinite-volume limits become uniform only after the length of the box is rescaled. We show that this rescaling, supplemented by an on-shell condition, defines a renormalization scheme. The whole dependence on the cut-off is absorbed into a factor $Z_L$ multiplying the length of the box, with an exponent fixed by the scaling dimension of the vertex operator; neither the field nor the coupling $β$ is renormalized, no subtraction scale is introduced, and the mass parameter receives a finite renormalization, fixed by requiring that the lightest breather has the mass of the boson in the linearized theory. The soliton and breather masses follow from the eigenvalues of the monodromy operator as functions of parameters that do not run, and reduce to the classical and semiclassical results as $β\rightarrow0$. In particular, the mass ratios are produced directly from the regularized construction, while the relation between the lattice parameters and the physical scale is absorbed into $Z_L$ and never needs to be computed. The scheme is a reparameterization of the theory which makes explicit the interplay between integrability and renormalization. We compare it with Coleman's normal ordering and with conformal perturbation theory, and we argue that it extends to ultralocal integrable theories with a massive spectrum, possibly including asymptotically free models that admit an ultralocal lattice regularization.
summary: This paper introduces a novel renormalization scheme for the sine-Gordon model by utilizing the quantum inverse scattering method on a lattice. The scheme successfully absorbs all cut-off dependence into a single rescaling factor, demonstrating that the theory's fundamental parameters remain unrenormalized. This provides a powerful, integrable perspective on renormalization, comparing it favorably against established methods like normal ordering.
main_problem: The paper develops a consistent renormalization scheme for the sine-Gordon (SG) model using the quantum inverse scattering method (QISM). This scheme aims to handle the cut-off dependence inherent in lattice regularizations.
main_result: The renormalization scheme absorbs all cut-off dependence into a single rescaling factor $Z_L$, leaving the field and coupling constant unrenormalized. The mass parameter receives a finite renormalization fixed by matching the lightest breather mass to the linearized boson mass.
method: The method employs lattice regularization of the SG model, followed by a rescaling of the box length and the imposition of an on-shell condition derived from the monodromy operator eigenvalues.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Sine-Gordon (SG) model, a 2D integrable field theory. It is analyzed via its lattice regularization and its continuum/infinite-volume limits.
key_observables: Soliton and breather masses, the renormalization factor $Z_L$, and the vacuum energy density.
important_parameters: The coupling constant $ eta$, the mass parameter $m$, and the lattice spacing $\delta$. The scheme is valid for $0 <  eta^2 < \pi$.
main_assumptions: The renormalization scheme is defined by the on-shell condition, and the authors argue it extends to ultralocal integrable theories with a massive spectrum.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes the quantization process across different physical systems (finitely many bodies, linear, non-linear). Other figures illustrate the flow from classical to quantum descriptions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the lattice regularization and the need for rescaling. It then details the renormalization procedure using the on-shell condition, comparing the results with Coleman's normal ordering and Conformal Perturbation Theory. Finally, it discusses the implications for general integrable theories.
why_interesting: While focused on a specific integrable model, the rigorous development of a non-perturbative renormalization scheme that bypasses standard RG flow techniques is highly relevant to understanding how scale invariance and quantum corrections interact in many-body quantum field theories.
